result.title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
result.summary: Specialist medical vision-language models (VLMs) are strong within their specialties but hard to unify: their training data are often private, and independently developed specialists cannot be assumed to share an architecture. Deploying these large models separately is costly. We present HuluOPD, an on-policy distillation recipe that unifies heterogeneous specialists into one lightweight VLM using only unlabeled prompts, without requiring reference answers or the specialists' training data. The lightweight model answers each prompt, and the specialist of the prompt's modality supervises its response; a continuation-aligned cross-tokenizer loss makes this possible even when they differ in architecture and tokenizer. We apply HuluOPD to five specialists, for ultrasound, pathology, optical coherence tomography, fundus photography, and dental imaging. To distill and evaluate them, we build HuluOPDCorpus, 914k unlabeled prompts, and HuluOPDBench, 47k held-out test items, from over 90 public datasets, and score all models under one protocol on 132k test items, including third-party benchmarks. A single model with 10% of the five specialists' combined parameters retains 94% of their question-answering performance, and one with 2% retains 89%. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of unifying heterogeneous medical specialist VLMs without requiring their training data or a shared architecture.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 HuluOPD，一种仅用无标注 prompt 的 on-policy 蒸馏配方，把五个异构医学专家 VLM（架构与 tokenizer 各不相同）统一进一个轻量 VLM，并用跨 tokenizer 的续写对齐损失让专家按模态监督学生自身的回答，在自建 914k 无标注语料与 132k 测试项上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 主线是医学多专才模型合并压缩而非视觉推理，但其在无参考答案条件下用专家监督学生自身生成的 on-policy 轨迹、并以续写对齐解决异构 tokenizer 的做法，可能为 LVR 中的轨迹监督与贡献分配提供可供核查的线索。
